title: File status 14 on a sequential READ of an RRDS with a too-small relative key item, 34 on a WRITE past the end of an ESDS, and 38 on an OPEN of a file closed WITH LOCK
shapes: AIXA AIXAFLK: SELECT SLOT-FILE ORGANIZATION IS RELATIVE ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL with RELATIVE KEY IS WS-SLOT-NO PIC 9(2), and SELECT LOG-FILE ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL over DD LOGESD (an ESDS); 0000-MAIN OPEN INPUTs SLOT-FILE, PERFORMs 1000-SCAN-SLOTS UNTIL WS-SLOT-STATUS NOT = '00' then 1100-SLOT-STATUS (tests '14'); OPEN EXTENDs LOG-FILE, PERFORMs 2000-FILL-LOG UNTIL WS-LOG-STATUS NOT = '00' then 2100-LOG-STATUS (tests '34'); CLOSE LOG-FILE WITH LOCK, OPEN INPUT LOG-FILE, PERFORM 3000-LOCK-STATUS (tests '38')
asserts: The two SELECTs are one file_control fact each: SLOT-FILE is org RELATIVE, access SEQUENTIAL, with relative_key WS-SLOT-NO (a PIC 9(2) item, so relative record numbers above 99 do not fit); LOG-FILE is org SEQUENTIAL. 1100-, 2100- and 3000- are each one units fact, PERFORMed once from 0000-MAIN as plain edges facts (1000- and 2000- are PERFORMed UNTIL), and each tests the FILE STATUS item named in its own SELECT (WS-SLOT-STATUS, WS-LOG-STATUS, WS-LOG-STATUS). At run time, the sequential READ of a relative file whose next relative record number has more significant digits than WS-SLOT-NO ends in 14 (high-order digit 1, at-end condition); a WRITE past the externally defined boundary of the ESDS ends in 34 (digit 3, permanent error); an OPEN of a file previously closed WITH LOCK ends in 38 (digit 3). No INVALID KEY phrase is coded, so status alone reports each condition.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A sequential READ statement was attempted for a relative file, and the number of significant digits in the relative record number was larger than the size of the relative key data item described for the file.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A permanent error exists because of a boundary violation; an attempt was made to write beyond the externally defined boundaries of a sequential file.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: An OPEN statement was attempted on a file previously closed with lock.

notes: Quotes are the Table 34 entries for 14, 34 and 38 from igy6lr40.pdf via pdftotext, joined across line breaks. Table 34 words 34 for a sequential file; an ESDS is the VSAM sequential file, and how many records fill the extent depends on the cluster's space, so the key asserts the status the loop ends in, not a count. The slot RRDS must hold a record numbered above 99 for 14 to occur; no JCL step runs AIXAFLK and the statuses are what IBM says for such a data set. 37 (open mode the file cannot support) and 44 (record size on REWRITE or a RECORD IS VARYING bound) are not planted: 37 depends on how the data set is allocated and 44 needs a variable-length FD this generator does not render. GnuCOBOL statuses were not compared.
